current_leader.name: Adaptive synthetic-monitor frequency optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: fixed synthetic schedule -> operational risk changes -> reduce eligible cadence/coverage within detection guardrails -> avoid billable runs -> restore cadence when risk rises
current_leader.why_survived: Still the strongest precise surviving vertical because billing is usage-linked, schedule mutation is out-of-path, and savings are measurable. This run did not find evidence sufficient to prove large marginal adaptive savings beyond best static tuning, so monetization is reduced and the candidate is now tied with the broader quota-boundary hypothesis rather than clearly ahead.
current_leader.closest_threat: First-party observability vendors possess both telemetry and schedule controls; static tuning may capture most savings.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read monitor definitions, periods, locations, run history and risk signals; recommend cadence changes; optionally mutate schedule through authorized provider API; measure avoided runs against best-static baseline.
current_leader.monetization: Per optimized monitor-month or capped share of verified savings incremental to a best-static baseline.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: No strong public evidence yet that dynamic adaptation creates material recurring savings after static cleanup.
current_leader.next_research_test: Obtain realistic enterprise synthetic estate distributions and calculate marginal adaptive savings versus best-static. Kill if adaptive increment is small. In parallel search for a new precise vertical that can exceed 45/60.

runner_ups.reason: Structurally strong but still lacks a precise high-value non-AI vertical.
Excellent recovery attribution but aggregate leakage and close reconciliation competition remain unresolved.
Real tradeoff but infrequent app-wide control weakens recurring monetization.

new_findings: IoT SIM dormant-subscription optimization initially scored well: machine-readable usage/status, explicit suspend/standby APIs, and direct basic-fee savings. Soracom documents Standby/Suspended states that can eliminate daily/monthly basic fees on eligible plans and API-driven state changes.

IoT SIM optimization is rejected as a new wedge because exact/near-exact products now exist. SIMWiser identifies idle active SIMs and quantifies savings; Spenza describes automated lifecycle engines that suspend silent SIMs; CMPs already expose activation/suspension/deactivation controls.
Toll/FASTag anomaly recovery remains rejected: current products reconcile GPS/toll data, detect double/wrong charges and prepare disputes.
Commercial insurance premium-audit automation is occupied by current AI audit platforms and payroll-connected premium systems.
The synthetic leader receives no economic promotion; absence of marginal-adaptive-savings evidence now reduces monetization confidence.
new_search_rules: A machine-readable state plus writable cost-saving control is insufficient if a current specialist already detects and acts on the same dormant state.
For adaptive optimizers, performance-fee attribution must use best-static configuration as baseline, not historical waste.
Do not let a leader persist merely because implementation is clean; if marginal economics remain unproven across repeated runs, reduce score and force promotion pressure.
